RichTextEditor from ui-components is a text area shown as a rich text editor, Tiptap, in the colors of the theme and the look of the page. Its toolbar formats the text: headings, bold, italic, underline, strike, code, the color of the text and of its background, links, lists, task lists, quotes, code blocks, lines, tables, images and alignment. In the drop-down Toolbar, choose its tools one by one: the Java making that toolbar shows below. The drop-downs Text colors and Background colors choose the colors of each palette, apart; with none chosen, the editor has no tool for them. The check box Keyboard keys adds a feature of the page's own, KbdFeature: keys such as Ctrl, with their tool, Ctrl+Shift+K and their script, which the cleaning lets through. The usual keys work too, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I or Ctrl+K for a link, and Markdown's marks as you type: # and a space for a heading, - for a list, **bold**. The toolbar is one stop of Tab: the arrow keys move along it. Escape, then Tab, leaves the editor, even in a list. A code block is in a language, which the menu of its tool chooses, and shows in its colors. An image comes from an address, or uploads: chosen in its form, or dropped or pasted into the text.

The server keeps the article in the session: its HTML, which it follows as you type, and the state of its editor, what you selected, how far you scrolled and the size you gave it by the bar along its bottom. It never trusts the HTML of the browser: it cleans it before it keeps it, keeping only what the features of the editor write. Below the editor, the article as a page shows it once saved, and the HTML the server keeps. Ctrl+S, or the button, saves it. The editor listens to the events the page gives it, through two Ajax behaviors whatever their number: Ctrl+S and the focus lost submit the form, the focus got and the size you give it go to the server alone, and the changes not saved mark the title of the page with a star, in the browser alone.

Below the second pill, the editor keeps Markdown instead of HTML. Below the third, HTML from anywhere, with scripts, handlers and styles, and what the cleaning leaves of it. Everything works under a strict Content Security Policy: the HTML has no style attribute, text aligns by classes.
An article in HTML, cleaned on the server

The browser checks the spelling as it does, or not, in the language of the text. The proofreader on the server underlines what it finds: click a word underlined, or press Ctrl+. for the next one, to choose a replacement or ignore it. Type @ and a name to mention someone, # and a topic, or the start of a word and Ctrl+Space for the terms that complete it: the server answers each list as you type.
This word may be spelled wrong.
The text as a page shows it
Keyboard keys, a feature of the page's own

Choose the language of a code block in the menu of its tool: Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON or Markdown, in their colors. Upload an image from the form of the image, or drop or paste one into the text: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, {0} at most.
Type, select, scroll or resize: the server keeps it all.

Format the notes as you like: the server keeps them as Markdown.

HTML from anywhere, pasted or sent by a browser that is not the editor: a script, handlers, a link to javascript:, a style covering the page and a frame. Clean it, and see what is left: only what the editor writes.
Type, select or resize: the app keeps the article and its state.
The HTML as the editor gives it. A server keeping it cleans it first, as Wicket's RichTextEditor does.
